package std::fifo

Buffering.

This file: Fifo (block-RAM friendly), FifoFwft (distributed RAM), ShiftFifo
(flip-flops) and Lifo. async.tern: AsyncFifo (two clock domains, Gray-coded
pointers). packet.tern: PacketFifo (commit/drop whole packets).

All FIFOs speak Stream<T> on both sides: `pop.valid` means `pop.data` already
holds the oldest entry (there is no separate read strobe), and `pop.fire()`
removes it. Depths are counted in entries; `count` reports the number of stored
entries.

Modules:
  pub module Fifo<T: type, Depth: uint = 16, AlmostFull: uint = Depth - 1>
      Synchronous FIFO built on a memory with a synchronous read port, so it
      infers block RAM.
  pub module FifoFwft<T: type, Depth: uint = 16, AlmostFull: uint = Depth - 1>
      First-word fall-through FIFO on distributed (LUT) RAM: `pop.data` is a
      combinational read of the oldest entry, so an entry is visible one cycle
      after its push.
  pub module ShiftFifo<T: type, Depth: uint = 4>
      Flip-flop FIFO for small depths (at most 8): entries shift toward the
      output on every pop, so `pop.data` comes straight from a register and no
      RAM is inferred.
  pub module Lifo<T: type, Depth: uint = 16>
      Stack (last in, first out) on distributed RAM.
  pub module AsyncFifo<T: type, Depth: uint = 16>
      Dual-clock FIFO: the standard clock-domain-crossing data path.
  pub module PacketFifo<T: type, Depth: uint = 64>
      Store-and-forward FIFO for packet streams.

Run `tern doc std::fifo::<Item>` for the details of an item.
